entries.author: Padmasambhava (quoted by Dudjom Rinpoche)
entries.quote: The truth of everything is the dharmakāya, which goes beyond the intellectual mind.
entries.edition: Rigpa Translations 2004; revised with permission, Lotsawa House 2026
entries.locator: Section 2, View; paragraph beginning “This rigpa, the indivisibility”
entries.context_note: Dudjom Rinpoche explicitly attributes this sentence to Guru Padmasambhava. It is a quotation within his exposition of appearance and emptiness, not independently verified against an earlier Padmasambhava text.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Candrakīrti
entries.quote:
Conventional truth is the method;
And the ultimate is its outcome.
Not knowing how the two truths differ,
Your thoughts will wander astray.
entries.edition: Translation 2004; revised 2025; version 1.0–20250618
entries.context_note: Complete verse on distinguishing conventional and ultimate truth; translator’s primary bilingual selection, not an unattributed quotation aggregator.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Uttamā (canonical attribution)
entries.quote: On the eighth, I stretched out my legs, having burst the mass of darkness.
entries.edition: Translation ©1997; Access to Insight BCBS edition, revised 4 August 2010
entries.context_note: Nun Uttamā describes attainment after instruction from a trustworthy nun and seven days of practice. “The eighth” refers to the eighth day, not an instantaneous guarantee.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0

entries.author: Seung Sahn
entries.quote: Moment to moment our job is to do bodhisattva action and help all beings.
entries.work: The Eleventh Gate - Man Gong’s Net
entries.translator: Not credited in the official English transcript
entries.edition: Kwan Um School of Zen teaching library, dated May 31, 1999
entries.locator: Final paragraph, sentence beginning “Moment to moment our job”
entries.context_note: Seung Sahn’s commentary on Man Gong’s kong-an; this is Seung Sahn speaking, not Man Gong. He connects non-grasping to concrete compassionate function.
entries.rights: Copyright retained; brief 15-word excerpt, no claim of open license

entries.author: Khenchen Ngawang Palzang
entries.quote:
The complete integration of emptiness and compassion
Is the naturally arising sign of progress on the path.
entries.work: Advice on Bending Mind Toward the Good
entries.edition: Lotsawa House version1.1–20241020; translation2024, editorial assistance Ninjyed N.T.
entries.locator: Two lines beginning “The complete integration”, following the stages of stabilizing awareness
entries.context_note: Author identifies inseparability of emptiness and compassion as a sign of practice progressing correctly, after discussing view, meditation and conduct. Not a promise of attainment from reading a sentence.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC4.0

entries.author: Vimalā (canonical attribution)
entries.quote: All ties — human & divine — have been cut. Having cast off all effluents, cooled am I, unbound.
entries.locator: Final stanza; PTS verses 72–76, closing verse 76
entries.context_note: Vimalā’s first-person account of awakening after renunciation, not a claim about the posting account. Effluents refers to mental defilements. Read complete poem before selection.
entries.edition: Access to Insight BCBS edition, revised 4 August 2010; translation ©1998
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated on source page; noncommercial attributed excerpt

entries.author: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Tayé
entries.quote:
Without grasping at compassion, realize its emptiness.
Compassion, the spontaneous energy of emptiness, will emerge.
entries.locator: Lines on relative bodhicitta, beginning Without grasping at compassion
entries.edition: 2015 translation; version 1.4–20260514
entries.context_note: Explains compassion and emptiness together after distinguishing ultimate and relative bodhicitta. Not an instruction to withhold practical help.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0; attributed noncommercial excerpt

entries.author: Nāgārjuna
entries.quote:
From phenomena which are exclusively empty,
There arise only empty phenomena.
entries.work: Verses on the Heart of Dependent Origination
entries.edition: 2008 translation; version 1.1–20250220
entries.context_note: Dependent arising of phenomena empty of inherent existence; verse 6 explicitly rejects nihilism.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0; attributed noncommercial excerpt

entries.author: Jetsünma Mumé Yeshe Tsomo
entries.quote: Train again and again, therefore, in intention and compassion.
entries.work: Guidance That Lights the Way to Liberation
entries.locator: Fourth stanza, final line, following the two aspects of bodhisattva commitment
entries.context_note: Instruction to repeatedly train in compassionate intention alongside wisdom, in the context of bodhisattva vows and an ethical foundation for Dzogchen. Does not promise liberation from reading a quote.
entries.edition: 2024 translation; version 1.1–20240628; Tibetan composition2000
entries.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0; noncommercial attributed excerpt

entries.author: Daehaeng Kun Sunim
entries.quote: All things constantly change every instant, so there is nothing to cling to.
entries.locator: Introduction, explicitly quoted passage beginning Believe in your foundation
entries.edition: Official Hanmaum Seon Center web text, accessed2026-10-04
entries.context_note: Within directly quoted instruction to entrust experience to the inherent foundation and observe. Surrounding subsequent sections are summaries; excerpt is from explicit quotation only.
entries.rights: Brief attributed13-word excerpt; no open license asserted; no other excerpt from this page

entries.author: Dudjom Lingpa
entries.quote: Mind is primordially empty, naturally luminous and unsullied.
entries.locator: Line beginning Mind is primordially empty, in final recognition instructions
entries.edition: 2024 translation; version1.0–20240208
entries.context_note: Dzogchen description of mind nature, followed by recognition as criterion of realization; not assertion that merely reading is realization.
entries.rights: CC BY-NC4.0; noncommercial attributed excerpt

entries.author: Zen Master Dae Kwang
entries.quote: This is the last meaning of a retreat -- wake up and help our world.
entries.context_note: Concluding purpose of retreat after investigation and releasing attachment to opinions. Sentence is Dae Kwang’s own teaching, not one of the article’s historical quotations.
entries.edition: Kwan Um School of Zen teaching library, dated July31 1997
entries.rights: Brief15-word attributed excerpt; no open license asserted; first excerpt from work

entries.author: Longchen Rabjam
entries.quote: Without focus, exert yourself in benefitting beings through compassion.
entries.context_note: Non-fixation paired with compassionate activity; surrounding stanza retains cause and effect, vows and both accumulations. Not a recommendation to neglect concentration or responsibilities.
entries.edition: 2014 translation, edited by Judith Amtzis, Jacqueline Bourbon and Monsieur “Fifi” Greywhiskers; version1.3–20240909
entries.rights: CC BY-NC4.0; noncommercial attributed excerpt

entries.author: Padmasambhava
entries.quote: Don’t mistake mere words to be the meaning of the teachings.
entries.locator: Publisher book page, first quoted passage, first sentence
entries.edition: Rangjung Yeshe Publications; 2004 edition ISBN9789627341208 bibliographic credit confirmed in Google Books
entries.context_note: Traditional treasure-text attribution to Padmasambhava. Publisher pairs this sentence with instruction to integrate practice into one’s own being. Book page does not identify the individual treasure revealer or printed page for this excerpt; no such locator is invented.
entries.attribution_status: Traditional treasure-text attribution, as presented by publisher
